items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: the World's Greatest Jazz Band was a great band because Bobby Haggart was a beautiful musician and arranger, he wrote for it, and Yank Lawson, who was the other leader

ctx.x: And so I took the letter, it was an offer to do a tour with the College Swing Band, incidentally, I go out with them very soon and do a tour of Germany in October.

And they offered a tremendous amount of money, there was no jazz player getting that kind of money playing in a band, and then I wanted, I thought for some years, going all out and become just a soloist and not being in a band and not being regimented any more, although the World's Greatest Jazz Band was a great band because Bobby Haggart was a beautiful musician and arranger, he wrote for it, and Yank Lawson, who was the other leader, was very nice to me and it was quite a nice thing and you had these marvelous…

We never spent a winter in the north, it was either in the Islands, or Mexico or Hawaii, California, wherever, so anyway, I showed to the letter to Bob and Bob said, 'See, Bud, we're just about to make the turn into success, I wish you'd stay and turn it down.'
